To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the use of leak prediction can improve the performance of symmetric motion-compensed MD codes for the delivery of video data over OFDM systems; (ii) a cross-layer design approach, which takes into consideration both the channel and the video coding parameters, can improve the performance and the robustness of the video delivery system; and (iii) the use of side information can reduce significantly the drift management problem in the construction of symmetric MD codes.
a cross-layer design approach to the design of MD video coding and transmission schemes is feasible and can provide significant performance gains in terms of video quality and bandwidth utilization.
the diversity order of wireless channels is an important parameter in designing MD coding schemes for video transmission over such channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a novel MD coding scheme that is specifically tailored to OFDM systems.
the development of a cross-layer design for the delivery of FGS video over OFDM systems.
the design of an n-channel symmetric MD coder and decoder for video delivery over OFDM systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have shown the feasibility of constructing motion compensated MD codes for FGS video delivery over OFDM systems, and have demonstrated the benefits of using the channel diversity order in constructing these codes.
the proposed cross-layer approach for FGS video transmission over OFDM systems is a promising approach for future wireless multimedia communications.
the proposed MD scheme can provide a significant gain in the overall performance of an FGS video transmission scheme over OFDM systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of leak prediction and partial prediction in conjunction with the use of side information, can improve the coding and transmission efficiency of the FGS video coder, and can reduce the drift problem associated with the symmetric motion-compensanted MD coding.
the proposed scheme can provide a significant performance enhancement for FGS coded video delivery over multicarrier systems.
we propose an n-channel motion compensated multiple description (MD)-based fine granular scalable video coding and transmission system, which is optimized to the physical channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the diversity order of an OFDM system can assist the design of the video coding layer, which can then be exploited to improve the overall performance of a cross-layer design for video over OFDM systems.

the use of side information, in the form of a diversity order, can significantly reduce the complexity of constructing symmetric motion compensated multiple description codes for video communications.
by exploiting the channel diversity order, the proposed MD coding scheme can be used to construct symmetric motion-compensating MD codes that are robust to packet losses.
